PART 1

Just to note, I used to help run a 501c3. It was about 4 years ago, some of the tax laws will have changed, but since then, I also have assisted in private audits and investigations of 501c3's which were suspected of being fraudulent, fronts for criminal activity or where the owners were using them as money-making schemes. Take that for what you will.

http://990s.foundationcenter.org/990_pdf_archive/463/463408143/463408143_201412_990.pdf?_ga=1.59417444.852503102.1447601114

1) Feminist Frequency waited until the very last minute to file this form. Even though this is the disclosure of revenue and expenses from 2014, they are legally allowed to delay filing of this form until well into 2015.

This is not unusual. Lots of charities will wait and even file for extensions. Every single year. I've seen it happen a lot. Nothing to see here.

2) Total contributions for 2014 were $411,929. Total expenses were reported as $64,264. Hence. the net revenue for the charity in 2014 was $384,329.

Yes. However, that is not the whole story. Something is missing here.

3) According to this report Anita Sarkeesian was the only officer paid during 2014. She was paid $18,885. "Other compensation" is reported as zero. According to this report Anita works 60 hours per week for Feminist Frequency.

However, you will find elsewhere that her compensation is reported $47,326. This is a common tactic. Report your salary below the poverty threshold and give yourself just enough benefits to bump yourself to a comfortable lifestyle. Keep reading.

3) Anita Sarkeesian and Katherine Cross are listed as the only two officers of the organization.

And yet 3 officers are listed. Who is the third? And why are they not named? They are supposed to be named if they have voting authority.

4) Feminist Frequency reports fundraising expenses of $26,344. What were these expenses? The report does not say.

And it won't.

5) Feminist Frequency reported $47,326 in salaries and employee benefits. This presumably includes the $18,885 that was paid to Anita Sarkeesian.

See above.

PART 2

6) What, exactly, does Feminist Frequency do? Do they actually have any programs in place that benefit the public? In the Statement of Program Service Accomplishments there is a single item, "STARTING UP OPERATIONS FULFILLING MISSION STATEMENT". That's it. No specific programs either current or planned and no specific accomplishments.

Yes, the mission statement is a problem. Mainly because there really isn't one.

7) Furthermore, in part III item 2, "Did the organization undertake any significant program services during the year which were not listed on the prior Form 990 or 990-EZ?" was checked No. In other words, even though their revenue went from around $13,000 in 2013 to more than $400,000 in 2014, no new programs or services were created with this boom in donations.

I'm not really worried about this. There are bigger issues with this tax form.

8) Feminist Frequency checked Yes when asked if they had more than $15,000 in expenses for professional fundraising services. Yet in schedule G Part I 2a they checked off No when asked if the organization had any "written or oral agreement with any individual ... in connection with professional fundraising services". This seems contradictory to me. What were the more than $15000 in "professional fundraising expenses" then?

Those professional fundraising services were to Sarkeesian. And there was an agreement with Kickstarter. But I don't know what the fees are with them.

8) Feminist Frequency loaned $14,227 to someone in 2014 (Part X Item 22). However, in Schedule L Part II Anita Sarkeesian is listed as having loaned the $14,227 to Feminist Frequency in 2014. Which one is it? And why would Anita Sarkeesian need to loan more than 14,000 dollars to organization that is sitting on more than $300,000? Which one was it? Was Anita Sarkeesian the giver or the recipient of the loan?

The loan went to Sarkeesian. These things always bother me. With legitimate charities, loans to officers are worrisome. Officers of legitimate non-profits are generally successful people with a track record who were brought in to manage the organization. With charities under the microscope...well, draw your own conclusions as to why someone would take out a loan from their own charity and not a bank.

EDIT: I erred. Sarkeesian loaned the charity money to keep it afloat. Allegedly. Despite being flush with cash at the end of the year, the 990 doesn't show that she was ever paid back. Normally this would be a red flag for money laundering. Very curious as to where she got the funds for this.

9) In Part XII Feminist Frequency states their financial statements were reviewed by an independent accountant. However, in the next item they state their financial statements were not audited by an independent accountant.

A review is not the same as an audit. When I was helping out with our 501c3, we were audited. EVERY MONTH. What Sarkeesian is doing is telling the accountant: "These are the numbers...do they add up?" The accountant may not even see her bank statements. For all we know there isn't any money in the account. THAT'S RIGHT. Her tax statements could be total bullshit.

10) Feminist Frequency checked Yes to Part IV item 18: "Did the organization report more than $15,000 total of fundraising event gross income and contributions on Part VIII, lines 1c and 8a? If "Yes, " complete Schedule G, Part II " However Schedule G Part II is blank. Which one is it? Did they raise more than $15,000 at a fundraising event or not? This might just be a mistake on their part. However it is emblematic of the sloppiness of this report.

Their fundraising event was the Kickstarter.

NOTES:

  1. Where is the Charter? While it doesn't necessarily have to be filed with the 990, they do have to have a Charter that specifies all the things they claimed on this tax form.

  2. Where are all of her expenses? She's been traveling all over the country. How is she paying for all of it. I mean these hosting organizations surely aren't paying for every single expense she's incurring. Is she buying new clothes for these events? I always look at the expenses of a charity because that's where these people really make mistakes. And they have nothing listed. Like...where are the rental expenses for their offices? Things like that. The expense report is where I have a real problem.
